text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent weekly newspapers The Guardian and Mmegi (The Reporter) on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Botswana Defence Force (BDF) was not a government in waiting, commander lietenant-general Seretse Khama Ian Khama said in Maun. "We are not going to use our guns for personal gains," he said on a tour of BDF camps. On his own future, he said he ad no intention of leaving the BDF.

- Two employees of the Department of Information and Broadcasting who are facing corruption charges arising out of allegedly false expense claims, are challenging the Constitutional authority of the Department on Corruption and Economic Crime to proseute them.
- The Botswana Building Society, with an asset base of 354 million pula, is seeking to operate as a commercial bank.

- The general manager of Botswana Railways, Amrithalingam Ramji, has been elected president of the Southern African Railways Association. He is also chairman of the Southern Afican Transport and Communications Commission.

- Botswana is to negotiate with all those countries that require its nationals to have visas to visit them in an attempt to waive the requirement, assistant minister for local government Margaret Nasha has told the House of Chiefs.
